The story relies heavily on summary and exposition rather than dramatized scenes. Because the narrative covers an entire academic year (from October to May) and even jumps forward several years at the end, the narrator largely compresses time and summarizes the dynamics of her relationships, her internal realizations, and the passage of the seasons. While there are brief, vivid moments that include snippets of dialogue and action—such as Lizzy's confession at the Barn, Martin folding shirts at the laundromat, and Johan's comment in the poetry seminar—even these moments are quickly absorbed back into the narrator's overarching retrospective commentary rather than unfolding as full, real-time scenes.
